Chemistry Ph.D.
Return to: Graduate Programs, Certificates, Specializations, Emphases
The Department of Chemistry at UMaine provides programs of study and research leading to thesis-based M.S and Ph.D. degrees, as well as a non-thesis M.S. degree. The graduate program offers a broad range of courses in the chemical sciences that prepare students for their research projects and real-world problem-solving. Research comprises most of the work in thesis programs where students publish their research in peer-reviewed journals and present at professional conferences.
For more information contact, Matthew Brichacek, Graduate Coordinator, mbrich@maine.edu or visit the program website.
Required Courses
Ph.D. students are required to take 21 classroom credit hours (including CHY 693 but excluding INT 601 or equivalent, CHY 698, and CHY 699). In addition, students are required to have a minimum of 5 thesis credits of CHY 699 and 1 credit of INT 601 or other course approved by the Graduate School to satisfy the Responsible Conduct of Research requirement. Students must be registered for at least 1 credit of CHY 699 in the semester they plan to defend their thesis. A student’s advisory committee must approve course selection.
CHY 693 - Graduate Seminar Credits: 1
CHY 698 - Graduate Research Credits: Ar
CHY 699 - Graduate Thesis/Research Credits: Ar
INT 601 - Responsible Conduct of Research Credits: 1
Additonal information:
A student’s advisory committee must approve transfer courses.
Students are expected to demonstrate competency in three out of four traditional disciplines of chemistry (Analytical, Inorganic, Organic, Physical) by earning a satisfactory score on the appropriate ACS national exam or by decision of the student’s advisory committee.
Grades of B or better are expected in all courses. The chemistry graduate faculty may approve credit for a C grade, upon recommendation from a student’s advisory committee. Students receiving more than two C grades (or lower) will be considered as not having made satisfactory progress toward completing degree requirements.
Students are required to present one seminar each year that they are in residence, except the first, up to a total of four seminars for Ph.D. candidates or a total of two seminars for M.S. students. Appropriate topics, suggestions for preparing and giving a seminar, and criteria for grading will be discussed by the faculty coordinating the seminar program.
The student’s research advisor and Chair of the Advisory Committee should be selected and approved by the Graduate Faculty by the end of the first semester of graduate study. A student must talk to at least four faculty members and obtain their signatures on the “Choice of Research Advisor” form before officially requesting an advisor. The Chair must be a Full Graduate Faculty member in the Graduate School, in Chemistry or have Cooperating Faculty status in Chemistry.
Electives
All students in the Ph.D. and thesis M.S. tracks are recommended to take a total of 6 credits of CHY 698 (Research) by the end of the fall semester of their second year in addition to courses.
CHY 502 - Chemistry Instructional Laboratory Leadership Credits: 0 or 1
CHY 523 - Advanced Polymer Chemistry Credits:
CHY 525 - Physical Chemistry of Polymers Credits: 3
CHY 531 - Structure and Mechanism in Biological Chemistry Credits: 3
CHY 541 - Topics in Advanced Analytical Chemistry Credits: 1-3
CHY 551 - Topics in Advanced Organic Chemistry Credits: Ar.
CHY 555 - Intermediate Organic Chemistry Credits: 3
CHY 556 - Theoretical Organic Chemistry Credits: 3
CHY 559 - Problem Solving In Organic Chemistry Credits: 1
CHY 560 - Physical Methods of Inorganic Chemistry Credits: 3
CHY 562 - Advanced Organometallic Chemistry Credits: 3-4
CHY 571 - Topics in Advanced Physical Chemistry Credits: Ar
CHY 578 - Nanoscience Credits: 3
CHY 583 - Advanced Wood Chemistry Credits: 3
CHY 661 - Topics in Advanced Inorganic Chemistry Credits: 1-3
To satisfy modernized interdisciplinary requirements, students will be allowed to select from appropriate science, math, and engineering courses University-wide. A student’s advisory committee must approve course selection.
Thesis/Research Requirements
All chemistry students must select a research advisor and advisory committee by the end of the first semester of graduate study and thereafter meet with the committee at least once each year.
Thesis M.S. and Ph.D. students must complete sufficient research to be able to write a thesis or dissertation of publishable quality. The dissertation particularly should give evidence of an exhaustive study of a specialized field and should be an authoritative statement of knowledge on the subject, as well as an original contribution to modern chemistry. A student’s advisory committee decides whether the quality of the thesis and research is acceptable.
Funding Options
The department will support, with a teaching assistantship, a research assistantship (from the research advisor), or a fellowship, a student in Good Standing for two and one half years for a thesis M.S. and four and one half years for a Ph.D. Additional semesters of support may be granted upon request. This commitment of support does not apply to students who have agreed to enter the program without support. A student in “Good Standing” is satisfying the requirements of his or her program by the appropriate deadlines, performing teaching duties satisfactorily (for TA’s), and is making progress in research satisfactory to the advisor and advisory committee.
